regions.name: The Wharves
regions.notes: The Long Wharf, the Pool and its quays: every ship that trades with Elsmoor comes in here.

regions.name: Guild Town
regions.notes: Inside the walls: brick and tile, the Exchange, the merchant houses, the Lantern Church.

regions.name: Southbank
regions.notes: Across the Ox Bridge: the yards, the slips, the tide mill and the rougher taverns.

regions.name: Outside the Walls
regions.notes: The West Gate road to Oxley Ford, the coach house, and the edge of the Sedge.

nodes.name: Pool Berth 1
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Pool Berth 2
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Pool Berth 3
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Wharf Berth 1
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Wharf Berth 2
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: The Exchange
nodes.notes: A great brick hall with a clock: the council of merchant houses that rules Brackwater meets here, and every cargo is priced on its floor.

nodes.name: The Harbour Office
nodes.notes: Harbour dues, ships' papers and the watch. The cells are underneath.

nodes.name: The Counting House
nodes.notes: Ledgers of every cargo in or out for two hundred years, and the island's charts.

nodes.name: The Factors' Hall
nodes.notes: Where captains and merchants sign contracts, and crews are hired.

nodes.name: The Lantern Church
nodes.notes: A tall brick church whose lantern tower is lit for ships coming in after dark.

nodes.name: The Pool Infirmary
nodes.notes: Healers for sailors and dockhands.

nodes.name: The Brackish Eel
nodes.notes: A crowded tavern on the Long Wharf: eel pie, cheap rum, and news from every port.

nodes.name: The Golden Bale
nodes.notes: A merchants' inn with good beds and a better cellar.

nodes.name: Harbour Chandlery
nodes.notes: Rope, canvas, pitch, lanterns and charts.

nodes.name: The Ship's Larder
nodes.notes: Victuals for the voyage, by the barrel.

nodes.name: The Ox Forge
nodes.notes: Anchors, chain and ship's iron.

nodes.name: The Green Bottle
nodes.notes: Physic and dyes.

nodes.name: The Cloth Hall
nodes.notes: The covered market on the wharf.

nodes.name: The Sedge Door
nodes.notes: A reed-cutter's hut at the edge of the Sedge, for goods that never saw the Harbour Office.

nodes.name: Brackwater Yards
nodes.notes: The yards that build Elsmoor's ships.

nodes.name: The Tide Mill
nodes.notes: A mill that grinds on the ebb.

nodes.name: Bonded Warehouse
nodes.notes: Goods held under seal until their duty's paid.

nodes.name: West Gate
nodes.notes: The gate onto the Oxley Road. Shut at dusk.

nodes.name: Mole Light
nodes.notes: The light at the end of the Mole.

nodes.name: The Oxley Coach House
nodes.notes: The coach for Oxley Ford, the Midway Inn and Haldeport leaves before dawn.

nodes.name: West Gate Stables
nodes.notes: Horses and mules for the Oxley Road.

shapes.name: Brackwater Roads
shapes.notes: The sheltered water off the Ox mouth where ships wait for the tide.

shapes.name: The Pool
shapes.notes: The walled basin at the river mouth, deep at every tide: Brackwater's harbour.

shapes.name: The Ox
shapes.notes: The Ox, broad and brown, navigable up to Oxley Ford.

shapes.name: The Strand
shapes.notes: Mud and shingle running south-west.

shapes.name: The Long Wharf
shapes.notes: The stone wharf along the north bank: bales, barrels and cranes.

shapes.name: Kalatecha Quay
shapes.notes: The quay along the Pool's north side, where the ships from Kalatecha tie up.

shapes.name: Salt Pier
shapes.notes: A stone pier into the Pool.

shapes.name: Wool Pier
shapes.notes: A stone pier into the Pool.

shapes.name: The Mole
shapes.notes: The breakwater sheltering the Pool's mouth, its light at the end.

shapes.name: Ox Bridge
shapes.notes: A stone bridge of seven arches, with a toll-house at its north end.

shapes.name: Guild Street
shapes.notes: The main street through Guild Town, from the West Gate to the Pool.

shapes.name: The South Road
shapes.notes: South-west along the coast to Kettle Cove.

shapes.name: The Oxley Road
shapes.notes: North-west along the river to Oxley Ford.

shapes.name: Wharf Market
shapes.notes: Wool, grain and timber down the Ox; wine, spice and cloth off the ships.

shapes.name: Exchange Square
shapes.notes: The paved square before the Exchange.

shapes.name: The Slips
shapes.notes: Two ships on the stocks and one in frame.

shapes.name: The Town Wall
shapes.notes: Brick walls with stone towers.

place.notes: Town plan laid out 2026-10-16 (no picture): the walled Guild Town and the Long Wharf on the north bank of the Ox, the Pool at the river mouth with its quays, piers and mole, Southbank's shipyards across the Ox Bridge. Brick and tile. Its story, people and buildings are placeholders until we go over them.

regions.name: The Hald
regions.notes: The inlet and its quays: the Deepwater Quay, the Fish Quay, the whalers.

regions.name: Old Town
regions.notes: Grey stone and slate stepping up from the Deepwater Quay: the Kirk, the Harpoon, the steps.

regions.name: Upper Town
regions.notes: Above the Fish Quay: Chart Square, the Chart House, the Wayfarers' Hall.

regions.name: Hald Head
regions.notes: The headland at the inlet's mouth: the fort and the light.

nodes.name: Deepwater Berth 1
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Deepwater Berth 2
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Deepwater Berth 3
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Fish Quay Berth
nodes.notes: A berth for any ship that comes in: the first in port without a berth of her own here ties up.

nodes.name: Haldfort
nodes.notes: A squat stone fort on Hald Head, its guns over the inlet's mouth. Whoever holds the fort holds the harbour.

nodes.name: Hald Light
nodes.notes: The last light before the open ocean. It burns all night, every night.

nodes.name: The Harbour House
nodes.notes: The harbour-master, ships' papers and the watch.

nodes.name: The Chart House
nodes.notes: Charts of the west, some drawn by captains who never came back. Its keepers buy new ones.

nodes.name: The Wayfarers' Hall
nodes.notes: Where voyages west are planned and crews are hired: the notice board is all ships wanting hands.

nodes.name: The Kirk of the Lost
nodes.notes: A sailors' kirk of black stone; its walls are carved with the names of the drowned.

nodes.name: The Sick House
nodes.notes: Beds, broth and a surgeon who has taken off more frostbitten fingers than he can count.

nodes.name: The Harpoon
nodes.notes: The whalers' tavern on the Fish Quay: loud, cold, and full of stories.

nodes.name: The Last Light
nodes.notes: An inn on the Steps with a view of the light; captains stay here before sailing west.

nodes.name: Gorran's Chandlery
nodes.notes: Rope, canvas, pitch and harpoons.

nodes.name: The Salt Loft
nodes.notes: Salt fish and ship's biscuit for long voyages.

nodes.name: The Iron Steps
nodes.notes: Ship's iron, harpoon heads and chain.

nodes.name: Old Hester's
nodes.notes: Remedies for the cold and the damp, and charms for the sea.

nodes.name: The Fish Hall
nodes.notes: The covered end of the Fish Market.

nodes.name: Below the Steps
nodes.notes: A cellar under the Steps where wreck goods change hands.

nodes.name: Haldeport Slip
nodes.notes: A slipway for mending ships, and building the odd whaler.

nodes.name: The Try-Works
nodes.notes: Where the whalers boil down their catch. You smell it before you see it.

nodes.name: The Ropewalk
nodes.notes: A long low shed where the rope is laid.

nodes.name: Inlet Watch
nodes.notes: A watchtower on the shore road.

nodes.name: The Whalebone Arch
nodes.notes: Two great jawbones over the top of Chart Street.

nodes.name: The Midway Coach House
nodes.notes: The coach across the moor to the Midway Inn, Oxley Ford and Brackwater.

nodes.name: Moor Road Stables
nodes.notes: Horses and ponies for the moor.

shapes.name: The Western Ocean
shapes.notes: Grey water running out to the edge of every chart.

shapes.name: Hald Head
shapes.notes: The rocky headland at the inlet's mouth.

shapes.name: Deepwater Quay
shapes.notes: The deep-water quay along the inlet's south side, where the big ships berth.

shapes.name: Fish Quay
shapes.notes: The fish quay along the north side: herring, cod, and the smell of both.

shapes.name: Long Pier
shapes.notes: A stone pier off the Deepwater Quay.

shapes.name: Whalers' Pier
shapes.notes: Where the whalers tie up and the try-works' barrels go down.

shapes.name: Harbour Street
shapes.notes: Up from the Deepwater Quay through the Old Town.

shapes.name: The Midway Road
shapes.notes: South-east across the moor to the Midway Inn.

shapes.name: Chart Street
shapes.notes: Up from the Fish Quay to Chart Square and the Upper Town.

shapes.name: The Steps
shapes.notes: Stone steps climbing from the inlet head to Chart Square.

shapes.name: Headland Road
shapes.notes: Out along the shore to the fort on Hald Head.

shapes.name: Fish Market
shapes.notes: The morning catch sold off the boats at the inlet's head.

shapes.name: Chart Square
shapes.notes: A windy square of grey flagstones with a great compass rose laid in brass.

shapes.name: The Kirkyard
shapes.notes: Stones for the men the sea never gave back.

place.notes: Town plan laid out 2026-10-16 (no picture): the Hald, a deep inlet that is the harbour, with the Deepwater Quay, the Fish Quay and the whalers' pier; Hald Head's fort and light at its mouth; grey stone and slate climbing the hill; the Chart House and the Wayfarers' Hall for voyages west. Its story, people and buildings are placeholders until we go over them.
